deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the preceding pages Grothendieck works with quantities S_p(A) for compact operators. The scaling S_p(λA)=λ^p S_p(A) used on this page shows that S_p(A) is the p-th power of the Schatten p-norm, i.e. S_p(A)=Σ s_n(A)^p. He had obtained an additive inequality by a complex-analytic route: Fredholm-type entire functions M_H(ρ), the Mellin-type formula ∫ log M(ρ) ρ^{-1-s} dρ = (λ(s)/s)·Σ s_n^s with λ(s)=π s/ sin π s, and a limit m→∞. That inequality is (14): S_r(AB) ≤ (r/p)S_p(A) + (r/q)S_q(B), where 1/r = 1/p + 1/q. He remarks that this is 'remarkable but not the one we seek'. This page turns the additive (Young-type) inequality into the multiplicative (Hölder-type) one by the standard homogeneity trick.

Step 1. Replace A by λA and B by μB (λ, μ ≥ 0). This gives (λμ)^r S_r(AB)/r ≤ λ^p S_p(A)/p + μ^q S_q(B)/q.

Step 2. Set a=S_p(A), b=S_q(B), c=S_r(AB). Then c ≤ inf over λ, μ of [aλ^p/p + bμ^q/q] / [(λμ)^r/r].

Step 3. Substitute x=λ^p, y=μ^q, α=r/p, β=r/q, so that α+β=1. Then c ≤ inf (αax+βby)/(x^α y^β). By homogeneity of degree 1 this equals inf {αax+βby : x^α y^β = 1}.

Step 4. The infimum is attained by a compactness argument (sublevel sets of ax+by in the quadrant are compact). At the minimiser the Lagrange condition is d(αax+βby) ∥ d(x^α y^β), which gives ax = by. Since α+β=1, the minimum equals ax.

Step 5. The margin and the next page finish the computation: with x^α y^β = 1 one gets x = (b/a)^β, so the minimum is a^{1-β} b^β = a^α b^β.

Conclusion: S_r(AB) ≤ S_p(A)^{r/p} S_q(B)^{r/q}, i.e. ||AB||_r ≤ ||A||_p ||B||_q. This is Hölder's inequality for Schatten classes, here derived via an entire-function (Fredholm-determinant) proof of the Young-type inequality followed by optimisation over scalings.
errors: The infimum should be taken over λ, μ > 0 (or x, y > 0); at x=0 or y=0 the quotient is undefined.
The compactness argument requires a, b > 0. If a=0 or b=0 the infimum is 0 and is not attained; the conclusion c ≤ a^α b^β = 0 still holds, but this case is not treated separately.

The compactness claim is loosely stated: what is compact is the intersection of {x, y ≥ 0, ax+by ≤ M} with the curve x^α y^β = 1 (closed, and bounded when a, b > 0). The written justification is sketchy but the conclusion is correct.
Notation slip: c = S_r(C) with C standing for AB.

ideas.what: Derive the multiplicative Hölder inequality for Schatten norms from the additive Young-type trace inequality by rescaling A→λA, B→μB and optimising (Lagrange multipliers).
ideas.modern_name: Homogeneity/scaling trick (Young ⇒ Hölder); Hölder inequality for Schatten p-classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schatten-class Hölder: von Neumann (1937), Schatten–von Neumann (1940s), Dixmier (1953); the scaling trick is folklore
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to eigenvalue/Fredholm material in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) or 'Produits tensoriels topologiques' (1955); unsure

ideas.what: Trace Young inequality S_r(AB) ≤ (r/p)S_p(A) + (r/q)S_q(B), with 1/r = 1/p + 1/q (stated on the previous page, used here).
ideas.modern_name: Trace (Schatten-norm) Young inequality; cf. the stronger matrix Young inequality of Ando (1995)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (follows from the Horn/Weyl majorant inequalities for singular values)

missed.claim: The overall route on these pages proves Schatten Hölder via growth of entire functions (Fredholm determinants) and a Mellin-type integral formula with constant π s/sin π s, then passes from the additive to the multiplicative form. The method is unusual, though the result is classical. This page itself is only the routine optimisation step.
missed.quote: Remplaçons dans cette formule A par λA, B par μB ... La borne inférieure est = a^α b^β i.e. c ≤ a^α b^β
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest only, as part of Grothendieck's 1953 function-theoretic approach to eigenvalue and singular-value inequalities; it is not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a standard scaling/Lagrange optimisation that turns a Young-type trace inequality into Hölder's inequality for Schatten classes. Both the result and the trick were classical by 1953.
transcription_corrections: The final display should read c ≤ inf over x, y > 0 of (αax+βby)/(x^α y^β) = inf over x^α y^β = 1 of (αax+βby); the transcription is essentially right.
The margin note reads (diagonally, partly struck): 'La borne inf... est ≤ a^α b^β ... i.e. c ≤ a^α b^β'.
The bottom line reads roughly: 'comme α+β=1, le minimum cherché est donc égal à ax = by ; compte tenu de la condition [x^α y^β = 1]'.
